We need to implement sumImbalanceNumbers.

Problem: Given array nums length n up to 1000, values range 1..n. Need sum of imbalance numbers of all subarrays. For each subarray, sort its elements, then count number of adjacent pairs in sorted version where difference > 1.

We need total sum across all subarrays.

Brute force O(n^3 log n) (n subarray O(n^2) each sort O(k log k)). With n <= 1000, O(n^3 log n) ~ 1e9 too high. We need a more efficient solution.

Observations: Imbalance number of a subarray is count of gaps > 1 between distinct consecutive values after sorting.

Consider sorted array of subarray; gaps >1 correspond to missing integers in [min, max] that are not present in subarray. Actually, for each missing integer between min and max (exclusive of endpoints?), each missing integer can cause more than one gap? Let's examine: In sorted unique? Wait duplicates cause zero difference which not >1, so duplicates don't affect imbalance. If we have duplicates, sorted array has equal values and diff=0; they don't contribute to imbalance. So imbalance essentially counts number of distinct values where between successive distinct sorted values there is a gap of at least 2 (difference >1). So if we consider the set of distinct values in subarray, sort them, then number of gaps >1 = (# distinct values - 1) - number of adjacent distinct values with difference ==1? Actually count gaps >1 = number of times successive distinct values have difference >=2. Equivalent to: For sorted distinct values v0<v1<...<v_{k-1}, imbalance = sum_{i=0}^{k-2} [v_{i+1} - v_i > 1].

Another viewpoint: For each integer x, consider its presence in subarray. Define contributions of missing numbers. For a subarray, the imbalance number equals (max - min + 1) - (#distinct elements) - (# of gaps of size exactly 1?? Let's derive.

Let distinct sorted values be v0,...,v_{k-1}. Define total span = v_{k-1} - v0 + 1 (the count of integers from min to max inclusive). Number of distinct elements = k. Number of missing integers in [min, max] = span - k.
